messages:
Sam W: quick heads-up — bringing up new reranker candidate rdrk-v3 (FP16 -> PTQ int8) and seeing a weird samplewise flip pattern on the holdout. ndcg@10 drops ~3.2% vs baseline, but the loss seems concentrated on short queries.
Priya (eval): can you paste the quick numbers and dataset name? is this prod-holdout or the new hd-holdout?
Sam W: prod-holdout-v2. quick diff:
```
Baseline (rdrk-v2-fp16): ndcg@10=0.742, mrr=0.431
Candidate (rdrk-v3-int8): ndcg@10=0.718, mrr=0.427
Samplewise flips: 4.1% of queries changed top-1, skewed to len<=6 queries
```
Priya (eval): interesting. low-length queries often hit tokenizer edgecases or priming/concat differences. did tokenization change between v2 and v3? any truncation/padding changes?
Marta I: also check kv-pack alignment and prefix caching — int8 bringups sometimes change packing and cause different attention offsets. runtime config identical?
Sam W: runtime config identical AFAICT. model conversion script used our usual PTQ pipeline + quick clamp. tokenizer should be same vocab, but I'll diff the preproc.
Ben L: also re-run with seed variance and per-query normalization off/on. sometimes scoring rescale interacts badly with int8. suggest small ablation:
```
1) rerun eval with --normalize-scores=false
2) run with original fp16 kernels but int8 weights (to isolate kernel effects)
3) compute samplewise_flip_rate and short-query NDCG separately
```
Priya (eval): can you attach the samplewise flip distribution? even a small histogram is helpful. if flips are concentrated on queries with many near-ties, may be calibration not relevance.
eval-bot: automated-smoke: ran quick smoke on prod-holdout-v2 (seed=42, 5k samples) -> samplewise_flip_rate=4.12%, flips_by_len={"<=6":68%, "7-15":24%, ">15":8%}, mean_score_delta=-0.028. full logs at /mnt/evals/1709998881/rdrk-v3-smoke.log
Sam W: thanks — uploading diffs to the run folder. I'll re-run ablations now and post results. tagging @Priya (eval) for follow-up.
Priya (eval): ok once you have ablation numbers let's check: tokenization diffs, normalization toggle, and a run with fp16 kernel float ops + int8 weights. also run small human eval on a 200-case stratified short-query sample (we care about perceived relevance flips).
Marta I: if we see kernel vs quant differences, I'll spin a quick dedicated node to reproduce without autoscale noise. ping me if you want hardware isolation.
Ben L: FYI if you need a faster turn, run a delta ablation computing ndcg@1/3/10 to see where gap concentrates.
Sam W: will do. will post updated numbers in this thread (expect ~30m). :thumbsup:
